Adobe today announced the launch of the AI Assisted Editor Beta, a brand-new selective editing mode in Photoshop that uses a simplified, prompt-based interface for image editing. Details are as follows.

Photoshop adds selective AI Assisted Editor

Adobe announced the launch of the AI Assisted Editor, a new Beta experience that replaces Photoshop's traditionally complex and detailed image editing tools with a prompt-based interface and simplified menus.

Users can access the AI Assisted Editor from a new toggle button in Photoshop's menu bar, and can also hide it in settings at any time.

Once users enter AI Assisted mode, they will see a simplified interface that includes the following tools:

The AI Assisted Editor includes:

Prompt to Edit: transform images using natural language prompts, without the need for complex manual edits. Remove Background: eliminate backgrounds, refine edges and customise images with just a few clicks. Generative Expand: expand image size and generate content that blends naturally into the composition. Remove Tool: remove unwanted objects and distracting elements while preserving the image's realistic texture. Generative Fill: add, replace or remove content using simple text prompts. Generative Upscale: increase image resolution while maintaining sharpness and visual quality. AI Markup: annotate images to visually express editing needs, generating more precise results.

The markup tool is particularly useful for users new to image editing, as well as experienced users who need to quickly sketch out concepts or fine-tune effects. Users simply need to draw or click anywhere on the image, then add natural language instructions such as "add more clouds", "change these shoes", or "add a banner that says ON SALE NOW".

Adobe Firefly will automatically make adjustments, and users can further fine-tune in AI Assisted Editor mode, or switch to the traditional professional editor to continue modifying.

Other details announced today

In addition to the new selective AI Assisted Editor Beta, Photoshop has also added prompt-based mask editing functionality, allowing users to roughly select image areas they want Firefly Image 5 to edit.

Adobe said this feature responds to some of the criticism of the existing prompt editor—the previous version sometimes degraded image quality, or produced results that didn't quite match the overall image in terms of lighting or subject angle.

Another new feature Photoshop launches today is a brand-new non-destructive layer tool for lighting adjustments, covering options for exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites and blacks. Adobe said: "It lets you get Camera Raw-grade results without leaving your Photoshop layers workflow."

The complete opposite of the mask-based editing tool is "Prompt to Edit", which allows users to enter prompts to modify the entire image, not just specific parts.

For example, users can turn a daytime scene into a night scene, or transform a rainy scene into a sunny one—this tool can do exactly that.

This new tool supports FLUX 2 pro, FLUX Context Pro, Gemini 3.1 (with Nano Banana 2), Gemini 3 (with Nano Banana Pro), Gemini 2.5 (with Nano Banana), GPT Image 2, as well as Adobe's own model, and will create a new layer providing two versions of the edited image.

Finally, Adobe also announced two other features aimed at bringing users "more control, less distraction":

Dynamic Text, Shapes and Paths: extends Photoshop's dynamic text functionality to any custom shape or path, allowing text to automatically adjust along curves and free-form layouts while maintaining formatting without manual adjustments. Stock Panel Integration: integrates over 900 million Adobe Stock assets directly into Photoshop in a dockable panel, making it easy for users to search, preview and use assets without leaving their workflow.

The AI Assisted Editor launches today in Beta, while the other tools are officially available to all users starting today.
